lanes.name: Data-only fills against fields the engine ALREADY reads
lanes.shape:
NO engine change. Four separate repairs, all of them writing shapes that already ship and are already consumed.

(a) RUNE DAMAGE PAYLOADS. `RuneDef.damage?: {dice, die, type, critPersistent?}` exists (types.ts:1762) and `flaming` proves it: {"dice":1,"die":"d6","type":"fire","critPersistent":{"dice":1,"die":"d10"}}. Verified in public/core.json: core.runes.astral / astral-greater / impactful / impactful-greater have NO damage key at all. Write astral + astral-greater = {dice:1,die:'d6',type:'spirit'}; impactful + impactful-greater = {dice:1,die:'d6',type:'force'}. The greater versions differ from the base only in target-side clauses (save DC, push distance), so the payload is identical.

(b) MISTYPED SPECIFIC MAGIC ITEMS. Verified in core.json: all five are itemType 'equipment' with category/group/damage/acBonus/hardness all absent. They are not engine gaps, they are broken records — a specific magic weapon or armour that the importer failed to type. Retype: greater-chainbreaker -> itemType 'weapon', base pick (category martial, group pick, damage 1d6 P), runes {potency:2, striking:1}; greater-dragons-tongue -> weapon longspear (martial, group spear, 1d8 P), runes {potency:2, striking:2}; greater-energized-shield -> itemType 'shield' with acBonus 2, hardness 8, hp 64, brokenThreshold 32, runes {reinforcing: minor}; greater-mitigation-mail -> itemType 'armor' chain mail (acBonus 4, dexCap 1, checkPenalty -2, speedPenalty -5, strength 3, group chain), runes {potency:2, resilient:1}; greater-reactive-mail -> same chain-mail block, runes {potency:1, resilient:1}. Copy the statistics from the base item record already in core.items so the numbers cannot drift.

(c) `removesWeaknesses` (types.ts:854) is read at derive.ts:928 as `db.feats[fc.featId]?.removesWeaknesses` — insulated-poppet IS a feat, so the field reaches it today. Write `removesWeaknesses: ['electricity','cold']`.

(d) FEAT_SITUATIONAL registry rows. Nine `*-calling` entries already ship (situationalBonuses.ts:2861-2952) in exactly the two-row spend/regain shape, and derive.ts:1192 already puts `c.mythicCalling` into ownedFeatureIds, so the lookup reaches these five the moment the rows exist. handlers-calling: spend [{kind:'skill',detail:'nature'}] 'to Command an Animal, spending a Mythic Point'; regain adds diplomacy. hunters-calling: [{kind:'perception'},{kind:'skill',detail:'survival'}] (Seek is Perception, Track is Survival). sages-calling and runelords-calling: [{kind:'skill',detail:'all'}] — Recall Knowledge / Identify Magic are not restricted by skill, and bookkeepers-calling already uses `all` this way. sagas-calling: spend performance + diplomacy, regain diplomacy only.

(e) COMPANION_MODS (companionGrants.ts:156) is keyed by the OWNER's feat id and already carries `speeds?: Record<string, number|string>` where the string 'land' means "equal to its land Speed". miraculous-flight = { kinds: ['vehicle'], speeds: { fly: 'land' } }.
lanes.readWhere: Nowhere new. (a) derive.ts:1486 and :1694 already read `db.runes[p]?.damage` when folding property runes into a Strike's damage. (b) deriveStrike (derive.ts:1441) returns null for anything not itemType 'weapon' and bails again if `w.damage` is absent, which is exactly why these five are inert; deriveAc/deriveShield read acBonus/hardness/hp/brokenThreshold. (c) derive.ts:928, inside the weakness gather. (d) situationalBonuses.ts FEAT_SITUATIONAL, consumed by hasFeatSituational/entriesFor at :3357. (e) companions.ts:344 and :355 iterate COMPANION_MODS against the owner's feat ids.
lanes.playerSees: An astral weapon's Strike damage line reads '1d8+4 slashing plus 1d6 spirit' — today it reads nothing extra. The five broken items become usable: the greater chainbreaker gets a Strike row, the mitigation mail gives AC, the energized shield can be Raised and Shield Blocked. A tsukumogami poppet with Insulated Poppet stops showing weakness 5 electricity. Five more mythic callings put a * on the right skills. A signature vehicle shows a fly Speed.
lanes.risk: Almost none — every one of these writes a field the engine is already looking for, which is why it ranks first. The only judgement call is (b): the five item records' statistics must be copied from the base item (pick, longspear, steel shield, chain mail) rather than typed by hand, or the app will ship a longspear with the wrong damage die. Two honest ceilings carried over from the existing calling rows: 'attempt the check at mythic proficiency' renders as a PHRASE because PROFICIENCY_RANKS stops at legendary, and the 'first time each day you critically succeed' regain half can only ever be a reminder because the app never sees a roll. Both are consistent with the nine callings already shipped, so this fill does not make them worse.

lanes.name: Scan owned CLASS FEATURES through every applier that is currently feat-keyed
lanes.shape:
One structural change, no new record fields except two. The engine has a systematic hole: a dozen appliers read `db.feats[fc.featId]?.X` or `FEAT_GRANTS[fc.featId]` and NOTHING ever looks the same field up on an owned class feature. Verified feat-only read sites:
  derive.ts:310  untrainedProficiency
  derive.ts:928  removesWeaknesses
  derive.ts:1227 choice.ownsFeature (choiceOwnedFeatureIds iterates c.feats only)
  derive.ts:1423 weaponTraits
  derive.ts:1807 unarmedTraits
  derive.ts:2086 bulkLimitBonus
  build.ts:2289 / 2403 / 2705 / 3699 / 3761  FEAT_GRANTS[fc.featId]
  build.ts:2661 spellListAdditions (content.feats[fc.featId] only)
  build.ts:3272 the languages IIFE (featLangs from feats, heritageLangs from heritages, nothing from features)

The fix is to move the rider fields off `Feat` onto `DefenseGrants` (which `ClassFeature` already extends) and give every applier a second pass over `ownedFeatureIds(c, db)` reading `db.classFeatures[id]?.X`. Add a shared `FEATURE_GRANTS: Record<string, FeatGrant>` fed through the SAME applier as FEAT_GRANTS so the two registries cannot drift.

Two new fields:
  DefenseGrants.preparedTacticsSet?: number    // a SET, not a bonus
  FeatGrant.extraSkillIncrease?: { level: number; options?: ProficiencyKey[] }[]

Data: master-overdrive {skills:{crafting:'master'}}; expert-tactician {skills:{'lore:warfare':'master'}, preparedTacticsSet:4}; master-tactician {skills:{'lore:warfare':'legendary'}, preparedTacticsSet:5}; legendary-tactician {preparedTacticsSet:6}; warfare-expertise {skills:{'lore:warfare':'expert'}}; thaumaturgic-mastery {extraSkillIncrease:[{level:17, options:['arcana','nature','occultism','religion']}]}; classFeatures.wildsong.grantsLanguages = ['wildsong'] (core.languages.wildsong is a real id).

PROOF THIS IS A REAL HOLE, NOT A GUESS: featGrantsAuto.ts:132 ships `'expert-overdrive': { skills: { crafting: 'expert' } }` and :197 ships `'legendary-overdrive': { skills: { crafting: 'legendary' } }`. Both keys are classFeature ids. Every FEAT_GRANTS lookup passes a featId. Neither has ever fired. The work was done and thrown away.
lanes.readWhere: build.ts:2399-2441 (the proficiency-grant pass) gains a second loop over owned features through the same body — but the owned-feature set is not computed until build.ts:2570, so it must be hoisted above the proficiency block, or recomputed there with the same recipe derive.ts:1152 uses. build.ts:3140-3143 (`preparedMax: 3 + preparedBonus` inside `if (ownsClass('commander'))`) becomes `Math.max(3, ...features.map(f => f.preparedTacticsSet ?? 0)) + preparedBonus`. build.ts:1469-1477 for extraSkillIncrease, so each extra pick is still capped by skillIncreaseCap(level) and still round-trips through buildFromCharacter (build.ts:3885-3914). build.ts:3272 for the language pass. derive.ts's six sites each take the same second loop.
lanes.playerSees: Crafting reads Expert at inventor 3, Master at 7, Legendary at 15 — all three have been silently missing. Warfare Lore reads Expert at commander 3, Master at 7, Legendary at 15. The Tactics card reads 'Prepared 0/4' at 7, 0/5 at 15, 0/6 at 19 instead of a permanent three, and the daily-prep tactics picker offers that many slots. A 17th-level thaumaturge gets one more skill-increase picker restricted to the four Recall Knowledge skills. Wildsong appears in every druid's Languages card. Each with its source named in the breakdown popup.
lanes.risk:
This lane is a PREREQUISITE for lanes 3, 4 and 5 — the inventor's 19 innovation modifications, the runelord sins and the wizard curriculum spell lists are all classFeatures, and none of them can ever fire until the appliers look at class features. Build it early or the later lanes have nowhere to land.

Two correctness traps. (1) preparedTacticsSet is a SET: `3 + set` yields 7/8/9. Take max(3, set) as the base so Efficient Preparation's +1 still stacks. (2) Turning on the feature-id pass switches on the two dead overdrive entries as a side effect — correct, but it CHANGES existing saved characters' numbers. Diff the key sets first: any id that is both a feat id and a classFeature id would fire twice (harmless, since grants only raise via maxRank, but know it). And make sure the `redundantFallback` path at build.ts:2425 ('already trained, pick another skill') is not triggered by a feature grant that is a genuine rank RAISE. (3) Read class features through ownedFeatureIds, never the raw class feature list, or a feature a class archetype suppressed will still grant.

lanes.name: Strike riders: add/remove traits, set or step the damage die, set or extend the range increment, and per-strike critical specialization
lanes.readWhere: derive.ts `weaponRiderTraits` (line 1420) — it loops `c.feats` only and returns a trait ARRAY, so it must be widened to return a modified WeaponItem (traits + damage die + range) and must also loop ownedFeatureIds reading `db.classFeatures[id]?.weaponTraits`; its only caller `deriveStrike` (line 1441) already holds the `inv`, so a `designated` match can test instanceId. The `range` clause lands a few lines later where deriveStrike already branches on `w.range` for the thrown/ranged attack ability. derive.ts `applyUnarmedRiders` (line 1804) is already called on natural attacks (:1850), on stance/form strikes (:1880) and on the baseline Fist (:1899), so every surface these records need is reachable with no new plumbing — but `fromRecord` needs the granting record id to travel with the strike, so GrantedStrike / NaturalAttack / StanceStrike each gain `source?: string`, stamped where build.ts collects grantedNaturals. Per-strike `critSpec` is checked in critSpec.ts alongside the existing groups/traits/bases filters. raging-thrower relaxes derive.ts's `rageStrikeRider`, which today returns null for any ranged Strike.
lanes.playerSees: This is the biggest visible change in the whole plan, because everything downstream reads `w.traits`: once a trait lands, it DOES things — agile changes the MAP steps, versatile-X offers the alternate damage type, deadly adds its crit die, the trait pills render on the strike detail popup. Concretely: the Fist row reads 1d6, drops 'nonlethal' and gains 'shove'. A blowgun reads 1d4 with deadly d4. A hand axe gains a 'Thrown 10 ft' line and its own ranged attack row. A tomahawk's increment goes up by 10. A shield bash's die steps up. An exemplar's shortsword reads 1d8. The inventor's innovation Strike finally lists parry / ranged trip / tethered — the entire content of 19 shipped class features that do nothing today. A raging barbarian sees rage damage on thrown Strikes.
lanes.risk:
OVER-GRANTING IS THE WHOLE DANGER and it is worst here. An unfiltered `weaponTraits` rider applies to EVERY weapon the character wields: a weapon inventor with Razor Prongs would get a tearing, tripping greatsword AND a tearing, tripping dagger; Humble Strikes without `categories:['simple']` is a silent damage buff on every weapon in the pack. Two rules: (1) `designated` must be REQUIRED with no 'first weapon' fallback — if nothing is designated the rider applies to nothing and the builder shows an unanswered-choice prompt; (2) die steps must not COMPOUND — a champion with Deific Weapon and Deadly Simplicity on one weapon gets ONE step (take the best single step, not the sum), or a d6 becomes a d10.

`fromRecord` fails CLOSED, which is the safe direction, but a mistyped id then looks identical to a working one — the applier should warn. `remove` naming a trait the strike never had also fails silently. `match.hands` reads ItemBase.hands, which is '1+' on several weapons — decide explicitly whether those count.

Three printed clauses stay honest-but-partial. modular-head's 'when you Interact to use the modular trait you may add or remove nonlethal' is a table action with no persistent state — the trait lands, the toggle is a note. rope-shot's 'tethered if thrown' must test for the thrown trait and must not apply to a projectile. hurl-at-the-horizon is gated on ikon IMMANENCE, which is unmodelled — the trait would be permanent unless it is shipped as a mode instead.

lanes.name: Designate an inventory item as "the" class item (innovation, weapon implement, bonded weapon, rune-copy source)
lanes.shape:
THE APP NEVER LINKS A CLASS CHOICE TO AN INVENTORY ITEM. `InventorBuild` (types.ts:916) stores an innovation TYPE and three modification ids and no item. The thaumaturge's weapon implement is not recorded anywhere at all. The wizard's bonded weapon likewise. That single absence is why 19 inventor modifications, both crit-spec clauses, the armour restat, the rune cap and Rod of Rule are all inert.

One mechanism, five users:
  InventoryItem.designations?: ('innovation' | 'weapon-implement' | 'bonded' | 'ikon' | 'rune-source')[]
  mirrored in BuildState (next to inventorArmorStats / inventorModifications, build.ts:139-142) so it survives a rebuild.
The picker is a dropdown on the relevant setup card (Inventor / Thaumaturge / Wizard) listing the character's own inventory.

Then the four consumers:
  DefenseGrants.critSpecWeapons gains `designated?: 'innovation' | 'weapon-implement' | 'bonded'`. Data: inventor-weapon-expertise {critSpec:true, critSpecWeapons:{designated:'innovation'}} (gate on innovationType==='weapon' in critSpecSources, not in the record); initiate-benefit-weapon {critSpec:true, critSpecLevel:5, critSpecWeapons:{designated:'weapon-implement'}} — the existing critSpecLevel field carries the 'at 5th level' clause exactly; rod-of-rule {critSpec:true, critSpecWeapons:{designated:'bonded'}}.
  ClassFeature.extraPropertySlots?: number, resolved per inventory instance (rune-capacity: +1 beyond the item's normal cap).
  ClassFeature.armorOverride?: Partial<ArmorItem> + a per-item armour proficiency override mirroring Proficiencies.weaponOverrides (heavy-construction rewrites the innovation armour to a printed heavy block: AC +5, Dex cap +1, check -2, Speed -10, Str +3, Bulk 3, group composite, bulwark + entrench, and sets its proficiency equal to the character's medium-armour rank).
  `copyRunesFrom` ALREADY EXISTS as InventoryItem.copyRunesFrom (types.ts:1941) with a full applier (derive.ts:1104 effectiveWeaponRunes) and a manual picker in InventoryTab.tsx:1028 — but the AUTOMATIC path is gated on `DOUBLING_RINGS`, a hardcoded two-id Set at derive.ts:1083. Replace that Set with an item flag (`ItemPassiveEffects.copiesRunes?: 'fundamental' | 'all'`) so blazons-of-shared-power (fundamental) and blazons-of-shared-power-greater (all, and suppresses the secondary's own runes) work. cutting-heaven-crushing-earth is the same mechanism pointed the other way: it makes invested handwraps a rune source for ONE designated wielded weapon, so it reuses the same flag with 'rune-source'.
lanes.readWhere: derive.ts `weaponMatches(strike, w)` at line 1347 — it narrows on group/traits/bases/melee only and returns TRUE for an unnarrowed entry, so an unfiltered crit-spec grant lights up EVERY Strike. It needs the strike's instanceId (already on Strike, derive.ts:1012) compared against the designation. `critSpecSources` (derive.ts:1329) already walks cls.features, so both inventor and thaumaturge records are found today — narrowing is the only missing piece. derive.ts:1083-1107 for the rune-copy flag. attachments.ts:102 and :123 (planAttach) plus ItemEditorModal.tsx:1270-1282 both spell the property-rune cap as `Math.min(runes.potency ?? 0, 3)` and must both read extraPropertySlots. deriveAc / findWornArmor for armorOverride.
lanes.playerSees: The chosen weapon's inventory card carries an 'Innovation' (or 'Implement', 'Bonded') badge. Critical specialization appears on exactly ONE Strike instead of none (today) or all of them (an unfiltered grant). The innovation accepts a fourth property rune. An inventor's power suit shows its real heavy-armour AC and penalties. A character wearing blazons sees the off-hand weapon's attack bonus and striking dice jump to match the main hand, without hand-editing copyRunesFrom.
lanes.risk:
Shipping `critSpec: true` on these records WITHOUT the `designated` narrowing would immediately grant critical specialization on every weapon the character holds — the field and the data must land in the same change, never separately.

This lane GATES the inventor half of lane 3 (7 modification records here, 19 in the family), so its cost is shared. But heavy-construction and rune-capacity are genuinely one-off consumers riding on the designation — if the designation is deferred, both drop to singletons.

One printed clause is unreachable: Rod of Rule's second half (a -2 penalty to the TARGET's saves) is target-side and stays prose.

lanes.name: Spell ACCESS additions — widen the list, the repertoire, the divine font, and the known rituals
lanes.readWhere: build.ts:2659-2667 — widen from the singular object to the array, walk ownedFeatureIds as well as c.feats (this is why lane 2 must land first: lust and pride are classFeatures). `as:'repertoire'` writes into the target SpellcastingEntry.grantedRepertoire; `as:'font'` appends to entry.font.allowed at build.ts:1971-1974; `as:'ritual'` feeds the same list SpellsTab.tsx:611 renders as the Rituals section — note build.ts:2998 currently FILTERS ritual spells out of addedSpells, so the ritual path needs its own channel rather than reusing that one. `from:'deity'` resolves against content.deities[details.deityId] the same way FeatChoiceDef kind:'domains' already does.
lanes.playerSees: Rewrite Memory appears in a druid's primal picker (Fey Caller already behaves exactly this way, so the surface is proven). Animal Form and Monstrosity Form appear as granted, castable spells in the animist's apparition entry. Every divine-font pip offers Heal OR Harm instead of showing the wrong spell on half of them. A cleric with Restorative Channel can spend a font Heal on Cleanse Affliction. Commune appears under Rituals as a spell you know. The runelord's chosen sin adds its ten ranks of spells to the wizard's preparation picker, marked as added by the sin rather than by the tradition.
lanes.risk:
'list' grants NOTHING by itself and players routinely read it as 'I have this spell' — the picker MUST label those entries as added-to-list, or this lane creates a support burden rather than removing one.

Blessed Blood's set is deity-dependent: a character with no deity gets an empty picker and the feat silently does nothing, so the builder needs a visible 'choose a deity first'. Aura Enhancement additionally depends on a Battle Harbinger divine font that is not built at all (battle-harbinger-dedication is absent from CASTER_ARCHETYPES) — the spells will have no font to widen, so this lane delivers half of that record and should say so.

lust/pride carry a second requirement beyond this lane: `runelord` is a classFeature whose CHOICE must own the chosen sin feature. FeatChoiceDef.ownsFeature exists (types.ts:665) but choiceOwnedFeatureIds (derive.ts:1221) iterates feats only, so it needs the lane-2 widening plus `choice: {flag:'sin', ownsFeature:true, options:[greed,envy,gluttony,lust,pride,sloth,wrath]}` hand-authored — nothing in the data marks the seven sins as a curriculum set. The printed lists have holes (Pride's 2nd-rank entry is missing a spell in the source text); author only ids verified present in core.json and leave the gap rather than guessing.

Ghost-Path's 'reduce the secondary casters by 1' is a table adjudication and stays as printed text.

lanes.name: Spell-slot completeness: cantrips, highest-rank-only slots, repertoire width, extra signatures, and slot TRADING at daily preparations
lanes.readWhere: build.ts, the `for (const bonus of spellSlotBonuses)` loop (~L2777). Three changes: (a) `add()` gains an `r === 0` branch raising the entry's cantrip capacity — the cap is `cantripsKnown(cls.id)` (spellcasting.ts:19) used at build.ts:1754 and :1916, plus `arch.config.cantrips` at ~L2879, so all three slices become `+ cantripBonus`, and the builder's cantrip picker in builder/shared.tsx must offer the extra slots; (b) `highestOnly` takes ranks[ranks.length - 1]; (c) MOVE THE WHOLE LOOP to AFTER the caster-archetype block (build.ts ~L2836-2905). Today it runs BEFORE that block is pushed, so `entryId: 'first-frost-casting'` resolves to nothing and Frozen Breadth is a no-op even with perfect data — first-frost / cathartic-mage-dedication / red-mantis-assassin-dedication ARE registered in casterArchetypes.ts, so the entries exist by then. The trading panel is a new Rest-sheet surface writing PlayState.slotTrades, resolved in play.ts applyPlay beside `resolvedItemPassives` (play.ts:289-298).
lanes.playerSees: Two more cantrip pick slots in the builder and two more cantrips on the Spells page. One extra slot chip at the oracle's top rank with its restriction printed beneath. The gelid-shard archetype pool one spell and one slot wider at every rank but its top two. A sorcerer designating two extra signature spells at rank 3 or lower, which then drive the existing 'cast at' heightening picker. A 20th-level bard whose entire repertoire is signature. A slot-trading panel at daily preparations.
lanes.risk:
`restriction` is a NOTE, not enforcement — Gifted Power's slot will accept any spell the entry can cast, so a player can quietly use it for a non-mystery spell. Flexible Spellcaster's cantrip line is printed as a SET ('four instead of three', 'five instead of four at 4th'), not an add; encoding it as a flat +1 over-grants at levels 1-3 relative to the printed table if cantripsKnown ever changes — encode it with the level step. `repertoireToo` on a PREPARED entry must be ignored, not silently mean slots.

The trading half is much larger than the adding half and could ship separately: adding (the first eight ids) is straightforward and mostly a loop-ordering bug fix; trading (the last four) needs a new Rest-sheet panel, per-slot flags and validation. If the batch has to be split, ship the adding half first — it is the cheaper two-thirds of the record count.

lanes.name: Archetype parity: honour a pick the archetype already recorded, and share the class subsystem it unlocks
lanes.shape:
Two halves with one root cause: class machinery is gated behind `ownsClass(...)` and archetype takers get nothing, even when the archetype ALREADY RECORDED THE PICK. Verified gate sites in build.ts: :1362 and :2261 kineticist, :2022 animist, :2623 alchemist, :3110 thaumaturge, :3134 commander, :3154 inventor, :3175 kineticist.

(a) DEREFERENCE A RECORDED PICK.
  derivedGrant?: {
    from: 'heritage' | 'subclass' | `classChoice:${string}` | `feat:${string}`;   // where the earlier answer lives
    prefix?: string; suffix?: string;      // how the answer becomes a record id: 'initiate-benefit-' + value
    collection?: string;                   // which core.json collection to resolve in
    as: 'feature' | 'feat';                // owned class feature (its DefenseGrants, effectChoices and
                                           //   situational stars then all apply for free) or a bonus feat
  }
The answers already exist: Thaumaturge Dedication records `dedicationImplement`, Barbarian Dedication records `barbarianInstinct`, Hellknight Dedication records its order, and Order Training already ships `effectChoices:[{id:'order', options:[chain|gate|godclaw|...]}]`. Data: implement-initiate {from:'feat:thaumaturge-dedication', prefix:'initiate-benefit-', as:'feature'}; instinct-ability {from:'feat:barbarian-dedication', suffix:'-instinct-ability', as:'feature'}; advanced-order-training {from:'feat:order-training', suffix:'-greater-benefit', collection:'hellknightOrder', as:'feature'}.

(b) UNGATE THE SUBSYSTEM. The condition becomes 'owns the class OR owns the dedication'. `ClassResource.feat` ALREADY EXISTS for exactly this — classResources.ts:29-31 documents it as 'archetype parity', and :48 / :60 / :74 already ship it for Rage, Panache and Ranger. So: give the alchemist's versatile-vials entry `feat:'alchemist-dedication'` and drop the `classId === 'alchemist'` gate on AlchemyPanel (quick-alchemy); expose inventorModificationOptions / INVENTOR_TIER_LEVEL to a character who owns inventor-dedication (basic-modification); let the implement pipeline (build.ts ~3110) assign an adept benefit to the THIRD implement when intense-implement is owned, instead of hardcoding 'never the third'.

(c) NEW RESOURCES ON THE SAME REGISTRY. sanguimancer-dedication and exorcist-dedication both introduce a currency other feats spend and nothing tracks either. Add to CLASS_RESOURCES with `feat:` gating: spirit wisps {id:'spirit-wisps', kind:'counter', refresh:'rest', feat:'exorcist-dedication', max:1} (enticing-dwelling doubles it to 2 — see lane 8); sanguimancy HP {id:'sanguimancy-hp', kind:'counter', refresh:'rest', feat:'sanguimancer-dedication', max:'@actor.level', cap:'2*@actor.level'}.
lanes.readWhere: build.ts ~L3110 (the thaumaturge implement pipeline, which today says 'never the third implement'), ~L3154 (the inventor block), ~L2623 (the alchemist's versatile-vial base). derive.ts ownedFeatureIds (line 1152) is where a resolved `derivedGrant` must join the owned set, so the granted record's own fields all apply with no further work. classResources.ts resourcesForCharacter (line 139-145) already ORs `isBaseClass || (r.feat && featIds.has(r.feat))` — it needs no change at all, only rows. AlchemyPanel's classId gate is in the sheet component.
lanes.playerSees: An archetype thaumaturge's implement shows its initiate benefit instead of a feature that names nothing; a full thaumaturge's third implement finally shows its adept benefit. An archetype barbarian gets Draconic Rage's damage / Animal Instinct's unarmed Strike. An Alchemist-archetype character gets the Quick Alchemy panel and a versatile-vial pip. An Inventor-archetype character is offered a basic modification in the builder. A Hellknight gets their order's greater benefit. Spirit wisps and sanguimancy HP appear as tracked pips on the sheet.
lanes.risk:
`derivedGrant` resolves an id by string concatenation, so a mismatch between the pick value and the record id fails silently — the resolver must warn on a miss rather than quietly granting nothing, which is the same failure mode this whole audit exists to undo.

Ungating a subsystem is not always the same as granting the class's full version: an Alchemist-archetype character gets Quick Alchemy but NOT the alchemist's advanced-alchemy item count, and the panel must reflect that or the archetype out-performs the class. Similarly the archetype's instinct ability is the instinct ability alone, not the instinct's later rage-damage scaling.

sanguimancy HP is temporary HP with a cap of twice level — it must not be modelled as ordinary temp HP that a rest wipes, since a rest is what GRANTS it.

lanes.name: Counter and allowance overrides — a record modifies a number the engine computes from a formula
lanes.shape:
A family of records whose entire content is 'that number the app already computes should be bigger', where the number comes from a hardcoded formula no record can influence. Verified formulas: snareAllowance(craftingRank) returns prepared 4/6/8 (snareFormulas.ts:25, called from builder/shared.tsx:1819); commanderFolioMax() in build.ts; ChoiceGroup.pickByLevel for ikons; item.capacity.bulk per container (derive.ts:2116-2127).

One registry rather than one field per counter, so a new counter is a row not a refactor:
  export const COUNTER_MODS: Record<string, { counter: CounterId; op: 'add' | 'mul' | 'set'; value: number; repeatable?: boolean }[]>
  type CounterId = 'snares-prepared' | 'snares-known' | 'commander-folio' | 'ikon-picks'
                 | 'container-capacity' | 'prepared-tactics' | 'spirit-wisps'
Data: plentiful-snares {counter:'snares-prepared', op:'mul', value:2}; ubiquitous-snares same; tactical-expansion {counter:'commander-folio', op:'add', value:2, repeatable:true}; additional-ikon and second-ikon {counter:'ikon-picks', op:'add', value:1}; pack-rat {counter:'container-capacity', op:'mul', value:1.5}; enticing-dwelling {counter:'spirit-wisps', op:'mul', value:2}; legendary-tactician {counter:'prepared-tactics', op:'set', value:6} (or via lane 2's preparedTacticsSet — pick ONE home, not both).

Each counter needs exactly one applier call at its existing computation site — the registry is the shared part, the plumbing is per-counter.
lanes.readWhere: snareFormulas.ts snareAllowance gains a second argument (the owner's feat/feature id set) so builder/shared.tsx:1819 passes it through. build.ts commanderFolioMax likewise. The ikon pick count is read where ChoiceGroup.pickByLevel is resolved in the builder's extra-choice section. derive.ts:2127 `loads[inv.instanceId] = { used, capacity: item.capacity?.bulk }` is the single place a container's capacity is published, so the multiplier applies there and every downstream check (the over-capacity drop block at derive.ts:2174, InventoryTab's drag canDrop) follows for free.
lanes.playerSees: A snare specialist's daily prepared-snare slots go from 4 to 8 (12 / 16 at higher Crafting), and the builder offers that many. Two more tactic slots in the folio per Tactical Expansion. A fourth (and fifth) ikon picker on the exemplar. A ratfolk's backpack accepts 6 Bulk instead of 4, and the over-capacity warning stops firing at the wrong point.
lanes.risk:
Order of operations must be fixed and documented, or `mul` and `add` fight: apply `set` first, then `mul`, then `add` — otherwise Plentiful Snares plus a hypothetical +2 gives a different answer depending on registry order. `repeatable: true` must read the number of times the feat was actually taken, which means the applier needs the feat's repeat count, not just its presence.

pack-rat's printed text limits the increase to MUNDANE containers and vehicles — the applier must exclude magical containers (a bag of holding) or it silently multiplies an extradimensional space. That filter is the difference between this being right and being a quiet cheat.

legendary-tactician appears in lane 2 as well. Decide once: the counter registry is the more general home, but preparedTacticsSet is already scoped to the commander block. Do not ship both.

lanes.name: State-gated grants: a level gate, a player-CHOSEN damage type, and a mode that grants a Strike
lanes.shape:
`whileActive` already exists on DefenseGrants (types.ts:297) as `{ state:'rage'|'panache'|'hunt-prey'|'unleash-psyche'; resistances?; senses?; immunities?; speeds? }[]`, ClassFeature already extends DefenseGrants, and resolveFormula already substitutes @actor.con.mod — so `[{state:'rage', resistances:[{type:'bludgeoning', value:'3+@actor.con.mod'}]}]` on an instinct WOULD work today. Three narrower things block it:

(1) NO LEVEL GATE. Raging Resistance is a 9th-level feature hung on an instinct taken at 1st. Add `whileActive[].minLevel?: number`.
(2) A CHOSEN TYPE CANNOT BE STATE-GATED. Giant, dragon and elemental instincts let you pick the energy type; EffectGrant (types.ts:399-414) can carry resistances but has no whileActive, and resolved picks land in Character.chosenEffects which deriveDefenses applies UNCONDITIONALLY (derive.ts:825). So the pick would grant a permanent resistance. Add `EffectGrant.whileActive?: DefenseGrants['whileActive']`.
(3) A MODE CANNOT GRANT A STRIKE. ModeDef (types.ts:1548-1611) carries resistances / weaknesses / immunities / senses / speeds but no strikes — while StanceDef (types.ts:1613+) does carry `strikes?: StanceStrike[]`. invoke-offense grants a 1d8 spirit brawling agile/finesse/magical unarmed Strike ONLY for the duration of Enter Spirit Trance. Add `ModeDef.grantedStrikes?: StanceStrike[]`, applied exactly where activeStanceDef's strikes already are (derive.ts:1880).

Also `whileActive[].speedPenalty?: number` for Wooden Rage's -10 ft.

skin-hard-as-horn is the fourth shape: a DAILY choice that grants. FeatChoiceDef.daily (types.ts:718) exists and 67 records already carry one, and the Rest sheet collects every one — but a FeatChoiceDef option is `{value,label,description}` and carries NO grant, so all 67 answers are recorded and nothing more. The grant-carrying shape is EffectChoice (types.ts:418), resolved once at BUILD time. Give EffectChoice `daily?: boolean` and add `Character.dailyEffects?: DefenseGrants` as the twin of chosenEffects.

Data: on each instinct feature, whileActive:[{state:'rage', minLevel:9, resistances:[...]}] — giant-instinct bludgeoning plus an effectChoices energy pick, ligneous-instinct its printed types, spirit-instinct void plus 'damage dealt by undead' (see risk). skin-hard-as-horn: effectChoices:[{id:'attuned', daily:true, prompt:'Damage type your skin is habituated against', options:[bludgeoning|piercing|slashing -> {resistances:[{type:..., value:'floor(@actor.level/2)'}]}]}].
lanes.readWhere: derive.ts `activeStateGrants(c, db)` at line 475 — it scans c.feats, c.heritageId and ownedFeatureIds but NOT c.chosenEffects; add that scan plus the minLevel filter there. The results already flow into deriveDefenses at derive.ts:802 with the 'only while that state is active' condition string, so the display is free. The speed penalty needs a hook in deriveSpeeds (derive.ts ~1975-2000, beside the stance and mode speed blocks, which is where the formula-valued speed sources resolve). For skin-hard-as-horn: play.ts applyPlay (:289-298) already resolves item choices made in play beside `dailyChoices: play.dailyChoices ?? ch.dailyChoices` — a resolveDailyEffects(ch, play, content) goes there; consumption is one line in deriveDefenses at :825 next to the existing chosenEffects push; the Rest-sheet picker (CharacterSheet.tsx:214-219, dailyChoicesFor / unansweredDailyChoices) must surface EffectChoice entries alongside FeatChoiceDef ones.
lanes.playerSees: With Rage toggled on, the Defenses card gains 'Bludgeoning 3 + Con — Giant Instinct · only while that state is active', clickable through to the existing resistance breakdown, and it disappears the moment Rage is switched off. Speed drops 10 ft while Wooden Rage is up. Enter Spirit Trance adds a Spirit Strike row to the Strikes page that vanishes when the mode is off. At daily preparations, 'Skin Hard as Horn — damage type your skin is habituated against' offers three chips, and the Defenses card follows the pick.
lanes.risk:
Put the resistance data on the TEN INSTINCT records, not on raging-resistance itself — the generic 9th-level feature names no damage type, so writing it there gives a barbarian an untyped resistance from a record that prints none.

Wooden Rage is OPTIONAL: 'you CAN increase the additional damage from 2 to 6', and only then do you take the Speed penalty. Modelling -10 ft as an unconditional whileActive penalises every ligneous barbarian who rages normally. That half belongs in a ModeDef (Wooden Rage) in the same exclusive group as Rage, not in whileActive.

spirit-instinct is only half deliverable: 'resistance to void damage' is a type and lands; 'resistance to damage dealt by undead creatures' keys off the ATTACKER's traits, which the sheet never sees — carry it as the __cond condition string the breakdown already renders.

Skin Hard as Horn's printed caveat — 'this resistance doesn't apply against critical hits' — is not expressible in IwrEntry; carry it as __cond too, so the player reads it where the number is. Its family is real and named: pelt-of-the-beast is the exact sibling (it already carries a choice and grants nothing), and planar-resilience, environmental-adaptability, demon-hunter, the-queen-mother, viridian-crown and endless-memories all record an answer today and apply nothing.

lanes.name: Daily temporary items the player picks (scrolls, elixirs, potions)
lanes.readWhere: The Rest sheet's daily-preparations surface, beside the existing advancedAlchemy panel — that panel is the template for the picker, the count display and the clear-on-rest behaviour. The resolved picks are written into PlayState and merged into the derived inventory in play.ts applyPlay (:289-298) alongside resolvedItemPassives, so the temporary items behave as real inventory (bulk, use counters, the Strike/consumable surface) without touching the build.
lanes.risk:
The ITEM FILTER is the whole lane and it is the part with no precedent — effectChoices can express a spellFilter but there is no item filter anywhere in the engine, so this is genuinely new machinery rather than a widening. Budget for it honestly.

`fromKnownFormulas` and `fromSpellbook` reach into other subsystems (the alchemist's formula book, the wizard's spellbook) and will return an empty picker for a character who has neither — the panel must say why rather than showing nothing.

The temporary items must be UNSELLABLE and must not count toward wealth, or a player can farm daily scrolls into gold. That is a real exploit this lane creates if the flag is only cosmetic.

horn-of-plenty is an ikon and a container in core.json, so its own record shape needs sorting out first (see risk on lane 1's typing repairs).

lanes.name: Extend ANOTHER record's option list
lanes.readWhere: One resolver, `optionsFor(recordId, flag, character, content)`, called wherever a choice's option list is built: the builder's ChoiceDetails / picker component, the daily-preparation choice collector for the two rune menus, Builder.tsx's domain enumeration, and deriveBlastStrikes for the blast types. Centralising it is the point — today each menu builds its own list inline, which is exactly why nothing can widen them.
lanes.playerSees: A champion's daily Blessed Armament menu shows seven runes instead of five. A Harbinger's shows thirteen. A cleric with Splinter Faith picks four domains that are not their deity's, and Domain Initiate then offers those four. A kineticist's Elemental Blast offers a second damage type per element.
lanes.risk:
`replace` and `add` on the same target from two different records is undefined — resolve replace first, then apply adds on top of the replaced list, and say so in the resolver.

splinter-faith's four domains must feed EVERY downstream domain consumer (Domain Initiate, Advanced Domain, the deity card), not just the first picker built, or the feat half-works in a way that is worse than not working.

The added options must be VALID picks in the target's own applier — adding 'astral' to blessed-armament is only useful if blessed-armament's applier can etch an astral rune, which depends on lane 1 giving that rune a payload.

lanes.name: Skill and Lore training from build selections that are not feats (apparitions, deity)
lanes.shape:
`SubclassOption.grants` (types.ts:980-984) accepts `skills?: SkillId[]` only, which cannot express a Lore at all — that is why every animist apparition's 'Apparition Skills' line is inert. Either widen to `ProficiencyKey[]` or add a sibling:
  grants?: { skills?: SkillId[]; weapons?: WeaponCategory[]; armor?: ArmorCategory[];
             lores?: string[] }   // NEW: Lore SUBJECTS ('farming', 'herbalism'), stored as lore:<subject> trained
Data on all 13 apparitions: custodian-of-groves-and-gardens ['farming','herbalism']; reveler-in-lost-glee ['circus','fortune-telling']; speaker-in-sibilance ['fortune-telling','mountain'].
The deity half needs NO new field: `Deity.skill` already exists (types.ts:1312 — sarenrae.skill = 'medicine') and is read by nothing.
lanes.readWhere: build.ts:1444-1455, `for (const o of grantOptions) { for (const sk of o.grants?.skills ?? []) (skills[sk]='trained'), locked.add(sk); }` — grantOptions (build.ts:1372) already includes ...extraOptions, so the apparition picks ARRIVE there; only the Lore loop is missing. Also update build.ts:3876, which rebuilds the granted-skill set so a granted skill is not double-charged against the class's free picks. For the deity: build.ts:1537-1558, immediately after the favored-weapon weaponOverrides block, add `if (usesDeity && deity?.skill) { skills[deity.skill] = maxRank(..., 'trained'); locked.add(deity.skill); }`.
lanes.playerSees: Farming Lore and Herbalism Lore appear as trained rows on the Skills tab of an animist who attuned that apparition, sourced to the apparition in the breakdown. A cleric of Sarenrae is trained in Medicine for free, without one of their class skill picks quietly vanishing into it.
lanes.risk:
`locked.add(...)` is load-bearing: without it the granted skill can be re-picked as a free class skill and the player silently loses a pick. That is the specific bug this lane creates if the second half is skipped.

The apparition Lores are printed as granted 'while attuned' and the app has no attunement state, so training them permanently over-grants for an animist who swaps apparitions. The animist class text does say you are trained in the apparition skills of ALL your apparitions, so a permanent grant is defensible — but it is a DECISION, not a derivation, and should be recorded as one.

This lane is 4 records here and 13 apparitions plus ~485 deities in the family, so its real reach is far larger than its batch count.

lanes.name: Companion and familiar grants from the owner's feats
lanes.shape:
COMPANION_MODS (companionGrants.ts:156) is a real registry keyed by the OWNER's feat id and iterated at companions.ts:344 and :355. It carries kinds / senses / maxHpBonus / flyEqualsLand / speeds / iwr / strikeRider / maturityFloor / abilityBoosts / skills — but not the two things these records need:
  CompanionMod.grantedStrikes?: StanceStrike[]   // NEW. billowing-wings gives winged animal companions a
                                                 //   'gust' ranged unarmed attack, 1d4 bludgeoning, 30 ft, air + propulsive.
                                                 //   companions.ts already FORMATS companion strikes; only the grant is missing.
  CompanionMod.familiarAbilities?: string[]      // NEW. The ability RECORDS already exist in core.familiarAbilities
                                                 //   (lightning-needles, lightning-armillary, path-of-the-tempest are all
                                                 //   real ids) and companions.ts:567 already maps ids to records for display.
                                                 //   Nothing attaches them, so the roster never shows them.
Data: billowing-wings {kinds:['animal-companion'], grantedStrikes:[{name:'Gust', dice:1, die:'d4', damageType:'bludgeoning', traits:['air','propulsive','range-increment-30','unarmed']}]}; lightning-rings-intervention {kinds:['familiar'], familiarAbilities:['lightning-needles']}; lightning-rings-overcharge {kinds:['familiar'], familiarAbilities:['lightning-armillary']}; tempest-clouds-speed {kinds:['familiar'], familiarAbilities:['path-of-the-tempest']}.
lanes.readWhere: companions.ts:344 and :355, where COMPANION_MODS is already iterated against the owner's feat ids — both new fields are consumed in that same loop. The granted strikes join the list companions.ts already formats; the familiar abilities join the roster read at companions.ts:567. No new plumbing and no new surface.
lanes.playerSees: A winged animal companion's stat block gains a Gust ranged Strike with its own damage and range. A familiar's ability list shows Lightning Needles / Lightning Armillary / Path of the Tempest with their full rules text, instead of a feat that names an ability the sheet never mentions.
lanes.risk: Genuinely small and low-risk — the registry, the loop and the display all exist. Two honesty notes: the granted familiar abilities must NOT be charged against the familiar's ability allowance (these are free additions, and the allowance is a separate number the app already tracks), or the feat costs the player a slot it was meant to give them. And tempest-clouds-speed's ability grants the OWNER a +10-foot status bonus to Speed when ACTIVATED — attaching the ability puts the text where the player can find it, but the Speed bonus is an activation and belongs in a mode, not in deriveSpeeds.

lanes.name: Languages: grants from any record, plus player-picked language slots
lanes.shape:
`DefenseGrants.grantsLanguages` already exists (types.ts:282 and :513) and is read for feats and heritages and for invested items via passiveEffects. Two gaps:
(1) class features are not scanned at all (that is lane 2's wildsong).
(2) NOTHING EXPRESSES A LANGUAGE CHOICE. 'You learn three new languages of your choice' has no home — and neither does Multilingual, the most-taken language feat in the game, which is equally unmodelled.
  languageChoices?: number | string    // NEW, on DefenseGrants so feats, features and items all carry it.
                                       // A formula string for linguistic-nexus: 'max(1, floor(@item.level/2))'.
Picks live in BuildState.featLanguageChoices keyed `<recordId>:<i>` and are added ON TOP of the Int/ancestry slot budget, exactly like grantsLanguages.
Data: gnome-polyglot {languageChoices:3}; pact-of-the-rune-dragon {languageChoices:10}; linguistic-nexus {languageChoices:'max(1, floor(@item.level/2))'}.
lanes.readWhere: build.ts:3272 — the `languages:` IIFE, which today unions ancestry-granted + the Int budget picks + featLangs (feats) + heritageLangs + invested-item passiveEffects.grantsLanguages + overrides.addedLanguages. Add a pickedLangs pass over build.featLanguageChoices. The builder renders the pickers with the existing `openChoiceOptions({ type:'language' })` (openChoice.ts:93), which already resolves the language list — so the picker UI is free.
lanes.playerSees: Three searchable language pickers on the Gnome Polyglot feat card, ten on Pact of the Rune Dragon, and a scaling number on the Linguistic Nexus relic card — with the picks in the Languages rail card on the sheet.
lanes.risk: Essentially none mechanically: languages are informational on this sheet, so a wrong answer costs nothing but accuracy. Two notes. 'Chosen from common languages and uncommon languages you have access to' cannot be enforced (access is a GM call) — offer common + uncommon with a note rather than pretending to gate it. And linguistic-nexus's count scales with the RELIC's level, not the character's, so the formula scope needs @item.level, which the item-passive resolver has and the feat resolver does not.

lanes.name: Speed arithmetic: add to a speed the character already has, and ignore a penalty
lanes.readWhere: derive.ts deriveSpeeds — `add` runs as a final pass AFTER the base grants, the stance block and the mode block, guarded on `speeds[key] > 0` so it never conjures a fly Speed from nothing. `ignoreArmorPenalty` / `reducePenalty` go at derive.ts:1926 where the worn armour's speedPenalty is subtracted and where encumbered is applied as -10.
lanes.playerSees: A winged character's fly Speed reads 30 instead of 25. A dwarf in full plate walks at 25 instead of 20, and the Speed breakdown popup shows the armour penalty struck through with Unburdened Iron named.
lanes.risk:
THIN: 2 records in this batch, which by the rule stated in the brief is barely a lane. It is kept as one because the shape is a family shape (every 'your fly Speed increases by' feat in the game needs it and none can be written today) and because the guard — never create a speed, only widen one — is the part that must be got right once rather than five times.

Unburdened Iron's second clause, 'reduce any OTHER Speed penalty by 5 feet', spans penalties the app models unevenly (encumbered is -10 and hardcoded; a stance's speedPenalty is separate). Applying it to encumbered is right; applying it to a stance's printed penalty is arguable and should be a documented decision, not an accident of where the hook lands.

lanes.name: Armor property runes with a mechanical payload
lanes.readWhere: `actsAs` is read where the worn armour's fundamental runes are resolved into the AC item bonus (deriveAc), taking max(etched potency, any actsAs potency) so a +1 echo on +2 armour does not downgrade it. `passiveEffects` is read in deriveBulk at derive.ts:2087, where limitBonus is summed today from FEATS ONLY (`if (f?.bulkLimitBonus) limitBonus += f.bulkLimitBonus`) — the same line lane 2 widens, so the two changes share a call site.
lanes.playerSees: Armour etched with Adamantine Echo gives its +1 item bonus to AC. Assisting armour raises the encumbered threshold from 5 + Str to 6 + Str and the maximum from 10 + Str to 11 + Str, and the Bulk bar moves accordingly.
lanes.risk:
THIN: 2 records, kept as a lane because the missing concept — an armour rune with any mechanical payload at all — is what blocks them both, and because `passiveEffects` on a rune is the general answer rather than a one-off bulk field.

`actsAs` must take a MAX against the etched fundamental, never a sum, or a character stacks a property rune's virtual potency on top of a real one. This is the same arithmetic trap as blessed-shield (see singletons) and they should be solved with the same helper.

lanes.name: Eidolon type abilities and shared eidolon magic
lanes.shape:
Every one of the 13 eidolon subclass options ALREADY carries the answer in its own description — dragon-eidolon prints '**Eidolon Abilities** *Initial* breath weapon; *Symbiosis* draconic frenzy; *Transcendence* wyrm's breath' followed by the full text. Nothing structures it.
  SubclassOption.eidolonAbilities?: { tier: 'initial' | 'symbiosis' | 'transcendence'; level: number; name: string; text: string }[]
Authored from each option's own description: 39 entries, 13 types x 3 tiers.
share-eidolon-magic is the adjacent half: the eidolon's innate spells from Magical Understudy / Adept / Master have no home either (those features carry no field), so there is nothing to project onto the summoner. It needs `EidolonConfig.innateSpells?: { spellId: string; uses: number }[]` populated by those three features before the feat can share them.
lanes.readWhere: rules/companions.ts, where the eidolon stat block is derived — today it produces only ability mods, unarmed Strikes, senses and defences. The gate is already available: ownedFeatureIds holds eidolon-symbiosis at 7 and eidolon-transcendence at 17, so a tier renders once its feature is owned. Displayed on the eidolon companion block in the sheet's companion component; the shared spells would join the summoner's innate entry with a shared use counter.
lanes.playerSees: An 'Abilities' section on the eidolon's stat block: Breath Weapon from level 1, Draconic Frenzy appearing at 7, Wyrm's Breath at 17 — each with its rules text, instead of two class features that say 'your eidolon gains a new ability' and name nothing.
lanes.risk:
BE PLAIN ABOUT WHAT THIS DELIVERS: reference TEXT on the right block at the right level, not computed mechanics. Nothing rolls a Breath Weapon.

Eidolon Transcendence's second half — '+2 to one of the eidolon's ability scores' — cannot be applied at all and should not be attempted: EidolonConfig.abilities (types.ts:1668) is a free-entry map of MODIFIERS the player derives by hand, so the app never computes an eidolon's scores, has no number to add 2 to, and nothing to validate against. The most the builder can honestly do at 17 is print a reminder beside the eidolon's ability fields. See the impossible bucket.

lanes.name: A subclass hands over LEVEL-GATED class features (the gunslinger deeds)
lanes.shape:
`SubclassOption.featureIds?: string[]` exists (types.ts:966) — it is the oracle-curse lane built during this audit — but it is applied with NO level check, so it can only ever express 'you get this from the level the subclass is taken'. Widen it:
  featureIds?: (string | { id: string; level: number })[]
  // a bare string keeps today's meaning: from the level the subclass is taken.
Then author each of the six gunslinger ways with its three deeds: way-of-the-drifter [{id:'into-the-fray',level:1},{id:'sword-and-pistol',level:9},{id:'...',level:15}], way-of-the-pistolero [{id:'vital-shot',level:1},...], and likewise sniper / spellshot / triggerbrand / vanguard.
lanes.readWhere: derive.ts ownedFeatureIds, lines 1200-1204: `const opt = klass?.subclass?.options.find(o => o.id === subId); for (const id of opt?.featureIds ?? []) if (db.classFeatures[id]) out.add(id);` — the loop needs `if (typeof e !== 'string' && e.level > c.level) continue;`. Every parallel gather in build.ts that walks the same option (focus spells, effect choices) needs the SAME filter, or a deed's focus spell arrives nine levels early.
lanes.playerSees: The way's advanced deed (Finish the Job, Spinning Crush, ...) appears in Feats & Features at exactly level 9, with its own description, action cost and any fields it carries — instead of 'Advanced Deed: you gain the advanced deed ability of the way you chose' pointing at nothing.
lanes.risk:
THE LEVEL GATE IS THE LANE. Authoring the deeds into today's featureIds without it would hand a 1st-level gunslinger their greater deed — strictly worse than the present inertness, because a wrong number is worse than a missing one.

1 record in this batch, 18 in the family (6 ways x initial/advanced/greater). If the batch count is the gate this is a singleton; it is kept as a lane because the widened field is what EVERY future subclass-grants-a-later-feature case needs, and there is no other way to write one.

lanes.name: Retune an existing spellcasting entry's tradition or key attribute; and put an ITEM in inventory
lanes.shape:
Two small shapes bundled because razmiran-priest-dedication needs both and neither alone reaches three records.

(a) RETUNE AN ENTRY. build.ts computes an innate entry's tradition and key attribute from the GRANTING SOURCE (Charisma by default) and nothing can retune it afterwards.
  entryRetune?: { entryId?: string; scope?: 'innate' | 'all' | 'from-source'; tradition?: Tradition; keyAbility?: AbilityId; useClassDc?: boolean }[]
Data: ancestral-mind {scope:'innate', source:'ancestry+heritage', tradition:'occult', keyAbility:'<psychic key>'}; razmiran-priest-dedication {scope:'from-source', source:'cleric-dedication', tradition:'occult'}.

(b) GRANT AN ITEM.
  grantsItems?: { itemId: string; quantity?: number; invested?: boolean; free?: true }[]
Data: razmiran-priest-dedication {grantsItems:[{itemId:'razmiri-mask', free:true}]} — the item exists (src/data/index.ts keeps 'razmiri-mask'). extradimensional-stash is the same field pointed at an inherent container: a 5-Bulk extradimensional space with no Bulk of its own; the app already models itemType 'container' with ignoredBulk and Character.inventory containerInstanceId, so the container behaves correctly the moment it is IN the inventory.
lanes.readWhere: (a) build.ts's spellcasting assembly, applied as a final pass AFTER every entry is pushed (which is after the caster-archetype block at ~L2836-2905) so a retune cannot be overwritten by a later push. (b) build.ts's inventory seeding, so granted items round-trip through buildFromCharacter and are not duplicated on every rebuild — the item needs a stable instanceId derived from the granting record id, or a rebuild adds a second mask every time.
lanes.playerSees: A psychic's ancestry innate spells cast as occult using the psychic's key attribute, with the right spell DC on the Spells page instead of a Charisma-based one. A Razmiran Priest starts with a Razmiri Mask in inventory. A 20th-level rogue has a 5-Bulk extradimensional stash they can drag items into, with the Bulk bar unaffected.
lanes.risk:
The granted-item instanceId is the whole correctness question: derive it deterministically from the record id, or every rebuild duplicates the item and a character accumulates masks. It must also be deletable without the rebuild resurrecting it, which means a suppression flag, not just a presence check.

razmiran-priest-dedication's re-traditioning applies only to spells gained THROUGH that archetype's Cleric Dedication — scoping it to 'all' would silently convert a multiclassed character's real divine casting to occult, which changes their spell list and their counteract checks. Scope is load-bearing here, not cosmetic.

lanes.name: A record modifies an item MODE: its duration, or one of its drawbacks
lanes.readWhere: Where an item mode is instantiated for a character — play.ts, in the mode-activation path that copies the ModeDef into activeModes. Adjusting at instantiation rather than at definition is essential: the ModeDef is shared content and must not be mutated, or one character's Extend Elixir doubles every character's durations.
lanes.playerSees: An alchemist's elixir pill reads '2 minutes' instead of '1 minute'. A 20th-level alchemist's mutagen modes show only the benefits, with the drawback line struck through and 'suppressed by Perfect Mutagen' beside it.
lanes.risk:
THIN: 2 records. Kept as a lane because 'a feat modifies a mode I already have' has no expression at all today, and the alternative is two hardcoded special cases in play.ts.

`doubleDuration` operates on a printed STRING, so it must parse '1 minute' / '10 minutes' / '1 hour' and re-render, and must FAIL VISIBLY (leave the string alone plus a note) on anything it cannot parse rather than silently doing nothing.

perfect-mutagen's printed scope is mutagens YOU CRAFTED, which the app does not track — suppressing on every mutagen the character drinks over-grants. Say so, or add a crafted flag when items enter inventory.

lanes.name: A second heritage's mechanical benefits
lanes.shape:
Both feats say the same thing: 'you gain the mechanical benefits of the <X> heritage you selected at 1st level' — for a character whose single `Character.heritageId` is the VERSATILE heritage that is the feat's own prerequisite. The first-level heritage was therefore never recorded anywhere, so there is nothing to dereference.
Two pieces:
  (1) A picker with nowhere to live today: `OpenChoiceFrom.type` gains 'heritage' with an `ancestry?` filter, so the feat can ask which awakened-animal / yaoguai heritage was chosen. The answer joins ownedFeatureIds.
