lanes.risk:
THIN: 2 records, but they are the same record twice and there is no third.

The real risk is double-counting: a heritage grant that the versatile heritage ALSO gives (a sense, a language) must raise rather than stack. Route the second heritage through the same maxRank/Set-union paths as the first rather than a parallel additive pass.

These two also expose a general question the audit should not answer by accident — whether the app supports two heritages at once, which touches the builder's heritage card, the sheet's ancestry line and every heritage prerequisite. Scope it explicitly to 'a second heritage granted by a feat' rather than 'heritages are a list now'.

singletons.why: A champion's HELD shield behaves as though it carried the reinforcing rune for their level (minor@1, lesser@7, moderate@10, greater@13, major@16, supreme@19), or +1 Hardness if it already has that rune or is a same-level Sturdy Shield. derive.ts computes shield Hardness/HP/BT from an ETCHED rune only (inv.runes.reinforcing, an ArmorRunes tier 1-6). Nothing else in the app grants a VIRTUAL rune to a held item, so there is no family. Shape: `virtualShieldReinforcing?: { byLevel: Record<number, 1|2|3|4|5|6> }` on ClassFeature, read where the held shield's runes resolve, taking max(etched, virtual) and adding +1 Hardness when they tie. Shares the max-not-sum arithmetic with lane 16's `actsAs` and should reuse that helper. The player would see the shield card's Hardness/HP/BT rise on its own, which IS the confusion risk — the source must be named on the card or it reads as a bug.

Upgrades the resistance an INITIAL inventor armour modification grants from half level to full level, and asks which one if the character has several. Its only sibling is incredible-resistance (the same for breakthrough modifications: dense plating / layered mesh / tensile absorption) — two records is not a lane. Shape: `resistanceUpgrade?: { among: string[]; to: 'level' }` on ClassFeature plus a pick, resolved where the source modification's resistances formula is read (derive.ts:857, resolveFormula(r.value, scope)). What makes it awkward: NO FIELD CAN REWRITE ANOTHER RECORD'S FORMULA, so the implementation has to re-resolve the named modification's entry rather than add one — the existing values live as `max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))` strings in effect-backfill.json.

Rewrites the inventor's innovation ARMOUR to a printed heavy-armour block (AC +5, Dex cap +1, check -2, Speed -10/0, Str +3, Bulk 3, group composite, bulwark + entrench) and sets innovation-armour proficiency equal to the character's medium-armour rank. Unlike the weapon modifications this is a whole-item stat OVERRIDE, not a trait rider, and there is exactly one record like it. Listed inside lane 4 because it depends entirely on the innovation designation; if that lane is deferred this drops here. Shape: `armorOverride?: Partial<ArmorItem>` on ClassFeature applied to the designated worn innovation in deriveAc/findWornArmor, plus a per-item ARMOUR proficiency override mirroring Proficiencies.weaponOverrides — armour has no equivalent today, so that is a second field for one record. power-suit and subterfuge-suit ARE real armour items in core.json, so the target exists.

One extra property-rune slot on the innovation beyond the item's normal limit (max four with +3 potency). The cap is `Math.min(runes.potency ?? 0, 3)`, spelled in exactly two places — attachments.ts:102 and :123 (planAttach) and ItemEditorModal.tsx:1270-1282 — and nothing else in the app ever changes it. Shape: `extraPropertySlots?: number` resolved per inventory instance (needs lane 4's designation), threaded through BOTH sites or the editor and the validator disagree. No other record in the game raises a rune cap.

A wizard thesis that restructures the spell-slot table at daily preparations: trade two slots of one rank for a bonus slot up to two ranks higher (as many times as you have slots, each bonus slot at a different rank), or trade any one slot for two extra cantrips. SpellSlotBonus can only ADD; there is no way to SPEND, and the trade is re-made every morning so it is play state, not build state. Listed inside lane 6 because it shares the slot-trading panel with spell-combination and master-summoner — on its own it is genuinely deliverable, genuinely large, and wanted by exactly one record. The other four wizard theses need nothing like it.

Extra precision damage on the SECOND (and at 19th, third) hit against your hunted prey in a round. THE AUDITOR'S NOTE IS WRONG: the base Precision edge IS modelled — derive.ts strikePrecisionRiders (lines 1266-1272) already emits '1d8 precision — * first hit vs hunted prey', scaling 1/2/3 dice at 11/19, gated on c.subclassId === 'precision' and the Hunt Prey toggle. So the deliverable change is ONE EDIT to that function's text for a character at 17+: '1d8 precision · * 2nd hit vs prey' (2d8 on the 2nd and 1d8 on the 3rd from 19). What can never be delivered is a NUMBER: the sheet has no per-round hit counter and never sees a roll, so this stays an annotation exactly as the base edge does. Its two siblings need nothing from this — masterful-hunter-flurry is the existing mapReduction lane and masterful-hunter-outwit is a plain bonus.

Grants the armor specialization effects for every armour category the character is proficient with — plate's physical resistance, chain's crit-to-hit conversion, and so on, all keyed to the WORN armour's group. Nothing in src models armor specialization at all: there is no match for it anywhere, no ArmorGroup effect table, and no surface on the armour card. It is a whole missing subsystem (7 armour groups x their printed effects) wanted by one record in this batch. Deliverable as `ARMOR_SPECIALIZATION: Record<ArmorGroup, {resistances?, note}>` consumed in deriveDefenses when the worn armour's group matches and the feature is owned — but cost it as a subsystem, not a field.

Two-tier weapon-group re-categorisation: bombs and martial firearms count as SIMPLE for proficiency, advanced firearms count as MARTIAL. FEAT_LANE_GRANTS.weaponFamiliarity takes an explicit weapon-id LIST plus ONE mirrorCategory, and core.json holds 172 bomb ids and 119 firearm ids across the two tiers — so the existing shape technically works but would need a 291-entry hand-authored list and could still only express one tier. The right fix is to let weaponFamiliarity match by TRAIT or GROUP with a per-tier mirrorCategory, which is a small change wanted by one record here; every other familiarity feat in the game names a handful of weapons and already works.

The feat gives the PLAYER a permanent rune slot ON THEIR OWN BODY holding one armor property rune whose effects apply to them. The app only etches property runes onto armour ITEMS in inventory. Shape: a virtual, unremovable armour-shaped host on the character that the existing rune-attach validator accepts, plus a picker for which rune goes in it. Genuinely deliverable and genuinely one-off — no other record grants a body-worn rune slot. Note it becomes markedly more useful after lane 16 gives armour property runes any payload at all.

An invested graft whose entire content is a permanent character capability: you can breathe underwater. passiveEffects covers senses / speeds / resistances / immunities and has no notion of BREATHING, and unlike every other water item this one grants no swim Speed to piggyback on. Shape: `ItemPassiveEffects.capabilities?: string[]` rendered as a line on the character's condition/capability rail. That field would eventually serve a family (water breathing, no need to eat or sleep, constant darkvision-in-fog cases) but only this record needs it today, and a capability the sheet merely PRINTS is close to prose — be honest that it is a display line, not a mechanic.

Raises mental resistance to 5 + the character's number of Hellknight archetype feats. hellknight-dedication ALREADY stores `resistances:[{type:'mental', value:'@actor.flags.system.hellknightArchetype.featCount + 1'}]` — the data is written and the formula substituter cannot resolve that path, so both records are inert for the same reason. The fix is one addition to resolveFormula's scope: a way to count owned feats matching a trait or archetype, e.g. `@feats.archetype('hellknight').count`. That is a small, general capability serving 2 records; it is a singleton only because no third record in this batch counts anything.

Hands the character Underwater Marauder and Water Sprint, but only once they meet each one's OWN prerequisite (trained / master in Athletics). grantsFeats applies unconditionally, so writing it today would give a 2nd-level monk the 7th-level Water Sprint. Shape: `grantsFeats` entries gain `whenPrereqMet?: true`, re-evaluated on every rebuild so the feat arrives the level the prerequisite is met. The engine already evaluates feat prerequisites for the builder's eligibility filter, so the predicate exists — it is the deferred-grant timing that is new. One record here; the shape would serve every 'you gain X, and Y when you qualify' feat.

Lets one specially treated item hold TWO active talismans at once. The app enforces the opposite: attachKind() and the host rule in attachments.ts allow a host at most one talisman, so this feat is actively CONTRADICTED by the engine rather than merely unmodelled. Shape: a per-instance `talismanSlots?: number` on InventoryItem set by the feat's designation pick, read in the attachments validator. No other record relaxes an attachment cap.

Constant enlarge as a permanent package: Large size, +5 feet reach, +2 status to melee damage, clumsy 1 until the Enhancement removes it. None of it reaches the sheet — the id appears only as a LABEL in the automaton core-feat option list. The sizeOverride and reach fields in build.ts would carry two of the four clauses; the +2 status melee damage is a strikeDamage rider that already exists; the clumsy is a permanent condition the app can apply. So it is four existing mechanisms wired to one record, which is assembly rather than a lane.

Listed inside lane 20 with extend-elixir. On its own: suppressing part of a shipped mode has no expression, and the printed scope (mutagens YOU CRAFTED) is not tracked, so any implementation over-grants unless a crafted flag is added when items enter inventory.

impossible.why: PARTIAL. The proficiency half already lands (advancement.ts, inventor level 11, source 'medium-armor-expertise-inventor'). The second sentence — 'access to the critical specialization effect with your armor innovation' — cannot. Armour critical specialization in PF2e fires when an ENEMY critically hits YOU and alters what THEIR attack does; it is not a number this character holds and not a roll this character makes. The app's entire crit-spec surface (critSpec, critSpecWeapons, strikeShowsCritSpec, derive.ts:1317-1362) hangs off a Strike row, and an armour innovation has no Strike. Building a weapon-shaped grant for it would put a crit-spec line on a Strike the rule does not touch. The most it can be is a note on the armour's item card.

PARTIAL. The ability half is covered by lane 17; the '+2 to one of the eidolon's ability scores' half cannot be applied. EidolonConfig.abilities (types.ts:1668) is Partial<Record<AbilityId, number>> of MODIFIERS the player derives by hand from the chosen array plus level boosts — the app never computes an eidolon's scores, so there is no number to add 2 to and nothing to validate against. At 17 the builder can print a reminder beside the eidolon's ability fields and nothing more. The free-entry design is what makes it unreachable; do not build a boost lane for it.

Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from Strikes made by frightened creatures, equal to FOUR TIMES THAT ATTACKER'S frightened value. The resistance value would have to be read from a creature the sheet has never seen and recomputed per incoming attack. IwrEntry values resolve against @actor only, and there is no attacker in scope anywhere in deriveDefenses. The most that can be delivered is a marked resistance line whose value is a formula string the player evaluates at the table — which is prose with extra steps. Genuinely a table adjudication.

PARTIAL. The critical-specialization half is covered by lane 4 via the bonded-weapon designation. The second half — a -2 penalty to the TARGET's saves — lands on a creature the sheet does not model and stays as printed text. Listed here so the half that cannot be built is not quietly forgotten inside the lane that builds the other half.

PARTIAL. The sanctification and ritual-knowledge halves are covered by lane 5. 'Reduce the number of secondary casters required by 1' is a ritual-casting parameter resolved entirely at the table — the app does not model ritual casting participants at all, and adding a participant counter to display one feat's -1 would be inventing a subsystem to hold a note.

PARTIAL. The modular trait itself lands via lane 3. 'When you Interact to use the modular trait you can also add or remove nonlethal' is an ACTION resolved at the table with no persistent state the sheet can hold — the trait arrives, the nonlethal toggle stays a note on the strike.

PARTIAL. The annotation change is a singleton-sized edit (see singletons). The NUMBER is impossible: extra damage on the second and third hit in a round requires a per-round hit counter and knowledge of the player's rolls, neither of which the sheet has or should have. The base Precision edge is already shipped as an annotation for exactly this reason, so this is consistent rather than a new limitation.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD

159 records. 21 lanes cover 146 of them; 11 records are singletons that no lane reaches; 2 are wholly impossible. Ten more records appear in BOTH a lane and the singleton or impossible bucket, because one printed half is buildable and the other is not — those are marked PARTIAL rather than silently rounded up.

Two of the four cluster proposals arrived truncated, so lanes for those quarters (g2 and g3 — 79 records) were rebuilt from the records themselves in work/lanes/all159.json rather than taken on trust. Every structural claim below was checked against the source before a lane was kept.

WHAT I DROPPED, AND WHY

Several clusters proposed lanes for things the engine already has. All were verified and demoted to DATA, which is why lane 1 exists and ranks first:
  - shadow-spells / forgotten-presence were flagged "there is no spell-list-addition lane". There is: spellListAdditions (types.ts:814), read at build.ts:2659-2667, consumed by SpellsTab.tsx:246-247. What is actually missing is only the array/feature/repertoire widening, which is lane 5.
  - insulated-poppet was flagged "every IWR field is additive". removesWeaknesses (types.ts:854) is read at derive.ts:928 and insulated-poppet is a FEAT, so the field reaches it today. Pure data.
  - astral / impactful and their greater versions were flagged as needing a rune-payload lane. RuneDef.damage exists (types.ts:1762) and flaming ships it; core.json simply omits the key on these four. Pure data.
  - The five mythic callings were flagged "unmodelled". Nine *-calling rows already ship in FEAT_SITUATIONAL (situationalBonuses.ts:2861-2952) in exactly the drafted shape, and derive.ts:1192 already puts c.mythicCalling into ownedFeatureIds. A registry fill, costed as data.
  - miraculous-flight's own cluster said it was a registry fill, and it is: COMPANION_MODS already carries speeds:{fly:'land'}.
  - blazons-of-shared-power was flagged as needing a rune-copy lane. copyRunesFrom exists (types.ts:1941) with a full applier at derive.ts:1104 and a manual picker in InventoryTab.tsx:1028. Only the AUTOMATIC trigger is hardcoded, as DOUBLING_RINGS at derive.ts:1083 — a two-id Set. Folded into lane 4.
  - masterful-hunter-precision's whyFlagged says "the base Precision edge is equally unmodelled". It is modelled: derive.ts:1266-1272 emits the 1d8/2d8/3d8 annotation gated on the precision subclass and the Hunt Prey toggle. Only the Nth-hit extension is missing, and only as text.

THE SINGLE BIGGEST STRUCTURAL FINDING

The engine has a systematic hole that no cluster stated as one thing: a dozen appliers read a field off a FEAT and nothing ever looks the same field up on an owned CLASS FEATURE. Verified sites — derive.ts:310 untrainedProficiency, :928 removesWeaknesses, :1227 choice.ownsFeature, :1423 weaponTraits, :1807 unarmedTraits, :2086 bulkLimitBonus; build.ts:2289/2403/2705/3699/3761 FEAT_GRANTS, :2661 spellListAdditions, :3272 the languages IIFE.

The proof it is a hole and not a design decision: featGrantsAuto.ts:132 ships 'expert-overdrive': { skills: { crafting: 'expert' } } and :197 ships 'legendary-overdrive': { skills: { crafting: 'legendary' } }. Both keys are classFeature ids. Every FEAT_GRANTS lookup passes a featId. Neither has ever fired. Someone already authored the data for a lane the engine cannot read. Lane 2 resurrects it, and lanes 3, 4 and 5 cannot land at all until it does — the inventor's 19 innovation modifications, the seven runelord sins and the wizard curriculum lists are ALL classFeatures.

THE SECOND STRUCTURAL FINDING

The app never links a class choice to an inventory item. InventorBuild (types.ts:916) stores an innovation TYPE and three modification ids and no item; the thaumaturge's weapon implement and the wizard's bonded weapon are not recorded anywhere at all. That single absence kills 19 inventor modifications, both crit-spec clauses, the armour restat, the rune cap and Rod of Rule. It is lane 4, and it is why lane 3's inventor half cannot ship alone.

THIRD: ownsClass() IS A WALL

Verified gates in build.ts at :1362, :2022, :2261, :2623, :3110, :3134, :3154, :3175. An archetype taker gets none of the class machinery even when the archetype ALREADY RECORDED THE PICK — thaumaturge-dedication stores dedicationImplement, barbarian-dedication stores barbarianInstinct, order-training stores the order. Meanwhile ClassResource.feat (classResources.ts:29-31) exists for exactly this purpose and already ships for Rage, Panache and Ranger. Lane 7 finishes a job the codebase started.

RANKING RULE APPLIED

Rank = (records covered) x (confidence it reaches the sheet), cheapest first among equals. That puts lane 1 (16 records, zero engine change, every field already read) first and lane 2 (6 direct records but a hard prerequisite for ~40 more, one afternoon of plumbing) second, ahead of lane 3, which covers the most records (29) but is the largest single piece of work and half-blocked on lane 4.

THIN LANES, DECLARED

Lanes 15, 16, 20 and 21 cover two records each, and lane 18 covers one. They are kept because in each case the missing CONCEPT — additive speed arithmetic, an armour rune with any payload, adjusting a mode you already have, a second heritage, a level-gated subclass grant — has no expression at all and the alternative is a hardcoded special case. Lane 18 is one record here and eighteen in the family (6 gunslinger ways x initial/advanced/greater), and the widened field is what every future subclass-grants-a-later-feature case needs. If a batch-count floor is imposed, these five are the ones that fall.

LANES WITH A SMALL SLICE HERE AND A LARGE FAMILY BEHIND THEM

Lane 12 is 4 records here, 13 apparitions and ~485 deities in the family. Lane 3's inventor half is 7 here and 19 in the family. Lane 9's daily-choice half is 1 here (skin-hard-as-horn) and ~10 in the family, with the siblings named: pelt-of-the-beast already carries a daily choice and grants nothing, and planar-resilience, environmental-adaptability, demon-hunter, the-queen-mother, viridian-crown and endless-memories all record an answer today and apply nothing. Sixty-seven records in total carry a FeatChoiceDef.daily whose answer the Rest sheet collects and discards, because a FeatChoiceDef option is {value,label,description} and carries no grant.

THE HONEST CEILINGS

"Attempt the check at mythic proficiency" renders as a PHRASE, not a number, in all fourteen calling entries — PROFICIENCY_RANKS stops at legendary. Making it compute is a rules-content decision about the proficiency ladder that would retroactively give a number to ~20 shipped entries; it is not a gap and is deliberately not in this plan.

Every "first time each day you critically succeed" clause is a reminder. The app never sees a roll.

Lane 3 is where over-granting is most dangerous: an unfiltered weaponTraits rider applies to every weapon the character wields, and an unfiltered critSpec grant lights up every Strike (derive.ts:1347 weaponMatches returns true for an unnarrowed entry). In both cases the FILTER and the DATA must ship in the same change, never separately.

BUILD ORDER, NOT JUST RANK

Lane 2 is a hard dependency of lanes 3, 4 and 5. Lane 4 is a hard dependency of the inventor half of lane 3 and of the two heavy-construction / rune-capacity singletons. Lane 1 depends on nothing and blocks nothing, so it can be done in parallel by whoever is touching data rather than code. Lane 16's actsAs arithmetic and the blessed-shield singleton share a max-not-sum helper and should be written once.
